summary: A is closer to the frozen contract because it preserves FilesService.Add unchanged and limits replayability to the new buffered Upload path. It is not merge-ready, but requires a smaller correction than B.
reasons: A uses internal/multipartbody.NewFile with the required field name and validates filename/content before request construction.

B intentionally changes Add by eagerly reading and buffering every caller-supplied body. That violates the explicit requirement to preserve Add behavior and changes memory, timing, and source-reader error semantics.
B’s Add retry test codifies that out-of-scope behavioral change.

B has substantially better Upload tests: it verifies field, filename, content, and an actual retry from an os.File. A only tests generic retry transport behavior and does not connect that verification to Upload.
risks_a: Upload duplicates Add’s option handling, request execution, response decoding, and missing-data error instead of routing through FilesService.Add as required.
The multipart test does not verify uploaded content.
There are no Upload tests for retry, empty filename, nil content, or source-reader failures.
risks_b: Add no longer retains its existing behavior: all custom multipart bodies are fully buffered and read failures receive new wrapping.
Upload calls the new private add helper rather than the existing public Add method, contrary to the contract’s required routing.
Tests omit validation and source-reader failure cases despite otherwise strong coverage.
